gate: 15 commercially plausible organizations/vendors/MSPs with recent EWS exposure; at least 5 with business-critical workflows

summary.note: This validates a real migration market, not automatic demand for a generic bridge. Several vendors already have Graph paths; those are migration-installed-base opportunities rather than product gaps.

targets.name: Fischer & Kerrn / Concierge Booking 365
targets.ews_signal: Current public material says Office 365 integration still uses EWS because Graph does not cover every required capability.

targets.name: Sign In Solutions Planner
targets.ews_signal: 2025 support documentation still instructs Office 365 users to connect Planner Display to outlook.office365.com/EWS/Exchange.asmx; 2026 release notes referenced EWS connectivity fixes.

targets.name: ResourceXpress
targets.ews_signal: January 2026 notice explicitly says SaaS and on-prem customers using Exchange Online through legacy EWS will stop synchronizing bookings unless migrated to Graph.

targets.name: Evoko / Evoko Home + Liso
targets.ews_signal: Current indexed product/security material describes Office 365/Exchange integration through native EWS and room booking/status synchronization.
targets.workflow: room status and direct booking from panels

targets.name: Johnson Controls OpenBlue Companion
targets.ews_signal: Product documentation lists Outlook/Office 365/EWS for integrated room booking synchronization.

targets.name: Crestron Fusion / Scheduling
targets.ews_signal: Crestron documentation historically used managed EWS for Office 365 scheduling; current ecosystem still carries EWS scheduling configuration, although newer paths may exist.
targets.commercial_angle: installed-base assessment; verify exact current Graph coverage before outreach

targets.name: AMX RMS-SCH-EWS
targets.ews_signal: Product page and July 2026 manual still describe an EWS scheduling interface; Office 365 modern auth now uses Graph.
targets.commercial_angle: migration installed base; not a pure feature-gap target

targets.name: Rise Up
targets.ews_signal: August 2026 migration guide says existing Office 365 calendar sync customers still running EWS must transition to Graph, with temporary EWS fallback.
targets.commercial_angle: evidence of migration complexity; vendor largely solving internally

targets.name: Wealthbox
targets.ews_signal: September 10, 2026 help article states Outlook calendar sync historically used EWS and customers must prepare for migration to Graph before October 1.
targets.commercial_angle: vertical CRM migration pattern; high-value regulated users

targets.name: Riva / Dynamics CRM on-premises customers
targets.ews_signal: August 2026 Riva article says Dynamics CRM on-prem built-in Exchange connection relies on EWS against Exchange Online and can lose email, appointments, contacts and task sync.

targets.name: The Access Group / OneOffice DPS
targets.ews_signal: August 2026 notice says DPS OAuth integrations connecting to Exchange Online via EWS need tenant action to avoid October interruption.

targets.name: Mimecast
targets.ews_signal: 2026 service notices say several products still depend on EWS: Threat Remediation, Sync & Recover, Continuity and parts of MSE.
targets.commercial_angle: large vendor internal migration; strong market signal, weak direct buyer fit

targets.name: Cronofy
targets.ews_signal: Current docs say some existing Office 365 EWS connections and individual/free-busy connections are affected and must move to Graph.
targets.commercial_angle: market proof and possible channel/partner intelligence

targets.name: OnTime Group Calendar
targets.ews_signal: August 2026 help article states older OnTime versions communicating with Exchange Online through EWS are affected; current versions support Graph.

targets.name: IBM services using Exchange Online
targets.ews_signal: June 2026 IBM service notice describes a phased transition from EWS to Microsoft Exchange Graph API for affected services/customers.
targets.commercial_angle: market validation rather than likely buyer

negative_controls.name: Flexopus
negative_controls.reason: Current Microsoft integration page explicitly separates Graph for Exchange Online and EWS for Exchange on-premises; not an Exchange Online EWS target.

negative_controls.name: Atlona Velocity
negative_controls.reason: April 2026 documentation says Graph is the current supported Microsoft 365 room-scheduling method.

negative_controls.name: CalendarBridge
negative_controls.reason: Current documentation says Microsoft 365 sync already runs on Graph and has no EWS dependency.

negative_controls.name: Zeeg
negative_controls.reason: Current documentation uses EWS only for Exchange on-premises and Graph for Microsoft 365.

conclusion: The commercial gate is satisfied. The strongest monetizable wedges are not a universal EWS proxy: (1) room/resource booking migration for legacy installed bases, (2) professional-services/practice-management integrations such as Access DPS, and (3) CRM/calendar sync for Dynamics CRM on-premises plus Exchange Online. Prioritize targets where the vendor has an active installed base but migration burden remains on customers or implementation partners.
next_test: Rank the A-priority targets by reachable buyer, installed-base leverage, migration complexity and evidence of unresolved customer burden; choose one where a fixed-scope rescue can be sold without building a public site first.
